public_rationale: On March 31, 2026, OpenAI announced a funding round with $122 billion in committed capital [e1]. That figure does not establish financing actually received during a complete annual period [e1]. The announcement documents neither an annual shortfall below $100 billion nor survival or funding-caused failure following such a shortfall [e1].
limitations: The evidence lacks a complete annual financing ledger, opening liquidity, and payment obligations.
The claim specifies neither an annual measurement convention nor a deadline for collapse.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will collapse unless it raises at least $100 billion a year.
conditions: if it fails to raise at least $100 billion a year

statement.excerpt: It needs at least $100 billion a year, or it’s toast!

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes this a claim about outside financing needed for survival, rather than revenue.
Read 'toast' as insolvency or cessation of normal operations caused by insufficient funding.
Count financing actually received by OpenAI, excluding unfulfilled commitments and secondary share sales whose proceeds go to shareholders.
The claim supplies neither an annual measurement convention nor a deadline for collapse.
criteria.support_condition: A complete annual period with less than $100 billion of financing received, followed by documented failure caused by the funding shortfall, would support the conditional prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented survival through a complete annual operating period with less than $100 billion of financing received would contradict the ordinary annual survival requirement.
